title: Find, Replace and Go To Special
summary: Wildcards, and selecting blanks, constants or formulas in one go.
objectives: Find and replace text across a sheet, safely.
Use Match entire cell contents and wildcards.
Select every blank (or every formula) with Go To Special, and fill blanks at once.

p: **Ctrl+F** finds; **Ctrl+H** finds and replaces. Type what to find, what to replace it with, then **Replace All**. Excel tells you how many replacements it made.
Before you click Replace All, think about what else might match. Replacing “Bombay” is safe; replacing “Bang” would also change “Bangalore Road” in an address.

visual.caption: Find and Replace with Match entire cell contents ticked

callouts.text: Replace All, after checking the options

p: **Match entire cell contents** only changes cells that hold exactly what you typed, so the city “Bangalore” changes but the address “12 Bangalore Road” doesn’t.
**Wildcards**: `*` stands for any characters and `?` for one character. `Sh*` finds Shah and Shaikh; `R?o` finds Rao.

head: Find
Matches
rows: Only cells that are exactly Bombay

check.q: You want to change the city “Bangalore” to “Bengaluru”, but an address in another column reads “12 Bangalore Road”. What do you tick?
check.explain: Entire-cell matching only changes cells that are exactly Bangalore.

slides.h: Select by kind, not by clicking
p: **F5** (or Ctrl+G) › **Special** selects cells by what they hold: **Blanks**, **Constants** (typed values), **Formulas**, errors and more.
It’s how you find every empty phone number in a list of 2,000 customers, or check which cells are typed numbers that should have been formulas.

slides.h: Fill every blank in one go
p: Select the column, then Go To Special › **Blanks**: only the empty cells are selected. Type the filler, such as *Not given*, and press **Ctrl+Enter**. Ctrl+Enter puts the entry into every selected cell at once.
The same trick fills blanks with 0, or with a formula like `=B2` that copies the value above.

check.q: You selected all the blank cells with Go To Special and typed “Not given”. Which key fills every selected cell?
check.explain: Ctrl+Enter enters the same thing into every selected cell.

demo.intro: Replace old city names across the list, carefully.

steps.say: Old names, “Bombay” and “Calcutta”, are scattered down column C. Press Ctrl+H to open Find and Replace.
Find *Bombay*, replace with *Mumbai*, Replace All: three cells change.
For Bangalore, tick **Match entire cell contents**, so “12 Bangalore Road” stays as it is.

demo.outro: Replace All is powerful. Entire-cell matching keeps it safe.

quiz.q: Which shortcut opens Find and Replace with the Replace tab ready?
What does `?` match in a Find?
quiz.explain: `?` is one character; `*` is any number.

quiz.q: What does Go To Special › Formulas select?
quiz.explain: Handy for checking which cells are calculated and which are typed.

quiz.q: Which key enters the same value into every selected cell?
Replace All changed “Pune” inside “Punekar Traders” too. What option would have prevented it?

points: **Ctrl+H**: find and replace across the sheet; check what else might match.
**Match entire cell contents** avoids partial matches; `*` and `?` are wildcards.
**F5 › Special › Blanks**, type, **Ctrl+Enter** fills every gap at once.
recap.cheat: Ctrl+H to replace, entire-cell matching to stay safe, Ctrl+Enter to fill a selection.
